props.title: Garden of the Gods Resort and Club
props.lede: Garden of the Gods Resort looks out over the red rocks of Garden of the Gods and up to Pikes Peak. It was a private club for decades, and it’s one of the most beautiful places in Colorado for a wedding.

headingText.html: It has seven event spaces with five terraces and lawns between them, and most of them look right at the rocks.

props.title: Live music in each Garden of the Gods Resort event space
props.lede: Here’s the act we’d pick for each space. Press play to hear it over the photo.

spaces.name: Reflection Pool
spaces.facts: The Reflection Pool is the resort’s main outdoor ceremony site, for up to 220 guests seated.
spaces.why: A solo violin to a full string quartet, from the ceremony through dinner.

spaces.name: Three Graces Ballroom and Terrace
spaces.facts: The Three Graces Ballroom is about 3,400 sq ft, for 220 to 300 guests. It has a glass-walled foyer and a private terrace with fire and water features.
spaces.why: He can start as a duo and grow to a full band over the evening.
spaces.alt: The Three Graces Ballroom set with navy-draped round tables and gold chairs.

spaces.name: The View at Kissing Camels
spaces.facts: The View at Kissing Camels is about 2,700 sq ft, for 130 to 150 guests, looking out over the golf course, Pikes Peak and the red rocks.
spaces.why: Country and Americana, solo, as a duo or with her five-piece band.
spaces.alt: The View at Kissing Camels set with round dinner tables in front of tall windows facing the mountains.
spaces.credit: Photo: Garden of the Gods Resort

spaces.name: Garden Room and Terrace
spaces.facts: The Garden Room is a ballroom with windows, about 1,900 sq ft, for 100 to 150 guests, and it can be divided.
spaces.why: Upright bass and guitar, at a volume nobody has to raise their voice over.

spaces.name: Hill Room and Terrace
spaces.facts: The Hill Room is round, with picture windows facing the rocks and the mountains, for 40 to 60 guests.
spaces.why: His own folk and Americana songs on acoustic guitar, solo or with his band.
spaces.alt: The round Hill Room set with long wooden tables and red napkins, with windows looking out toward the rocks.
spaces.credit: Photo: Garden of the Gods Resort

props.title: Planning music at Garden of the Gods Resort

rows.text: Our acts bring their own sound system, sized to the space. The resort also has full AV support for events.
Every wedding has a planner or coordinator, and we plan load-in and setup with them and the resort’s sales and catering team.
The resort caters events in-house, and the reception includes a dance floor.
The Reflection Pool and the terraces are outdoors, and the resort offers backup space for an outdoor ceremony.
There’s complimentary valet and self-parking at the resort.

props.html: Questions to ask the Garden of the Gods Resort events team

items.html: Which spaces have an end time for amplified music, and when is it?
Does the hotel’s AV team need to connect or run the band’s sound, and is there a fee for that?
Where do vendors load in, and when can the band set up?
Is there power near where the band will play?
What wording do you need on the certificate of insurance?

props.html: Forward this list to the events team, or send us the answers and we’ll plan around them.
Questions about music at Garden of the Gods Resort

items.q: Can we bring our own band to a wedding at Garden of the Gods Resort?
items.a: Hotels like Garden of the Gods Resort generally let you book your own entertainment, within their rules on insurance, load-in and sound. Your event manager can confirm them for your date, and we send a certificate of insurance with every booking.

items.q: Does the band need the resort’s AV team?
items.a: Our acts bring their own sound system, sized to the space. The resort’s AV team can add anything beyond that, and we’ll work out the details with your event manager.

items.q: Can one act play the ceremony, the cocktail hour and the reception?
items.a: Yes. The same act can move with you from The Reflection Pool to The Three Graces Terrace to The Three Graces Ballroom, and one booking covers all of it.

items.q: How much does live music add to a wedding at Garden of the Gods Resort?
items.a: It depends on the size of the act and how much of the day it covers. Our pricing page has what live music costs in the Colorado market, and we’ll send a quote for your date.
